item.title: 자큐보가 끌고 디지털 헬스가 민다…동아에스티 성장축 다변화 - 핀포인트뉴스
item.description:
요약

  • 동아에스티가 위식도역류질환 치료제 자큐보의 성장과 효율적인 비용 관리에 힘입어 3분기 수익성을 크게 개선했다.
  • DS투자증권은 핵심 전문의약품 사업의 성장세가 이어지는 가운데 일본 바이오시밀러와 디지털 헬스케어 사업까지 확대되고 있어 중장기 성장 기반이 강화되고 있다고 평가했다.
  • 전년 동기 대비 매출은 4.1%, 영업이익은 27.7% 증가했다.

본문

동아에스티가 위식도역류질환 치료제 자큐보의 성장과 효율적인 비용 관리에 힘입어 3분기 수익성을 크게 개선했다. DS투자증권은 핵심 전문의약품 사업의 성장세가 이어지는 가운데 일본 바이오시밀러와 디지털 헬스케어 사업까지 확대되고 있어 중장기 성장 기반이 강화되고 있다고 평가했다.

동아에스티는 올해 3분기 별도 기준 매출액 2065억원, 영업이익 214억원을 기록했다. 전년 동기 대비 매출은 4.1%, 영업이익은 27.7% 증가했다. 영업이익률은 약 10.4%를 나타냈다.

매출은 시장 예상치인 2203억원을 약 6.3% 밑돌았지만 영업이익은 예상치 128억원을 67.2% 웃돌았다. 매출 성장보다 수익성 개선이 두드러진 실적이다. 효율적인 판매관리비 집행과 연구개발(R&D) 비용 집행 시점이 늦춰진 것이 영업이익 증가에 기여했다.

핵심 성장축은 전문의약품(ETC) 사업이다. 3분기 ETC 부문 매출은 1559억원으로 전년 동기 대비 7.3% 증가했다. 2024년 3분기 도입한 위식도역류질환 치료제 자큐보가 성장세를 이어가면서 사업부 실적을 뒷받침했다.

자큐보의 3분기 매출은 220억원으로 전년 동기 대비 53.8% 증가했다. 출시 이후 시장 안착에 성공하면서 동아에스티의 주요 성장 품목으로 자리 잡고 있다는 평가다. 위식도역류질환 치료제 시장에서 처방 확대가 이어진다면 ETC 사업부의 추가적인 외형 성장도 기대할 수 있다.

기존 핵심 품목인 성장호르몬 치료제 그로트로핀도 경쟁 심화 속에서 안정적인 매출을 유지했다. 3분기 매출은 364억원으로 전년 동기 대비 1.1% 증가했다. 글로벌 제약사 노보노디스크가 성장호르몬 치료제 소그로야를 출시하는 등 경쟁 환경이 달라졌지만 기존 시장에서 견조한 판매 흐름을 이어갔다.

그로트로핀은 동아에스티의 주요 매출 기반이라는 점에서 의미가 크다. 신제품 자큐보가 성장 동력을 제공하는 가운데 기존 주력 품목이 안정적인 매출을 유지하면서 사업 포트폴리오의 균형을 뒷받침하고 있다.

해외사업부는 다소 부진했다. 3분기 매출은 392억원으로 전년 동기 대비 3.9% 감소했다. 경기 침체 영향으로 캔 박카스 등 일부 제품의 판매가 줄어든 탓이다. 다만 일본 바이오시밀러 매출이 증가하고 있다는 점은 긍정적이다. 기존 해외사업의 단기 부진을 새로운 바이오시밀러 매출이 보완하면서 중장기 사업 구조 개선 가능성을 보여주고 있다.

디지털 헬스케어 사업도 새로운 성장 분야로 떠오르고 있다. 3분기 매출은 28억원으로 아직 전체 실적에서 차지하는 비중은 작지만 전년 동기 대비 403.6% 증가했다. 성장률만 놓고 보면 주요 사업부 가운데 가장 두드러진다.

동아에스티는 디지털 헬스케어 사업 확대를 위해 제품군도 넓히고 있다. 지난 9월 초에는 심박수와 호흡, 체온, 산소포화도, 혈압 등을 측정할 수 있는 하이카디 M350을 출시했다. 다양한 생체정보를 측정하는 의료기기를 통해 디지털 기반 의료 서비스 시장에서 사업 영역을 확장하려는 전략이다.

디지털 헬스케어는 의약품 중심의 사업 구조를 보완할 수 있다는 점에서 주목된다. 고령화와 만성질환 관리 수요가 증가하면서 환자의 건강정보를 지속적으로 측정하고 관리하는 의료기기 및 디지털 서비스의 중요성이 커지고 있기 때문이다. 향후 제품 판매 확대와 의료기관 및 관련 서비스와의 연계가 이뤄진다면 새로운 매출원으로 성장할 가능성이 있다.

다만 3분기 영업이익 개선에는 판관비 절감과 연구개발 비용 집행 이연 효과가 반영됐다는 점을 고려해야 한다. 향후 연구개발 투자가 정상화되면 비용 부담이 다시 커질 수 있다. 자큐보의 처방 확대와 그로트로핀의 경쟁력 유지, 일본 바이오시밀러의 성장세가 지속되는지도 확인해야 할 부분이다.

증시에서는 동아에스티의 사업 구조가 기존 주력 의약품의 안정적인 매출을 바탕으로 신제품과 해외사업, 디지털 헬스케어로 확장되고 있다는 점에 주목하고 있다. 자큐보의 고성장과 일본 바이오시밀러의 매출 확대가 이어진다면 단기적인 비용 절감 효과를 넘어 지속적인 이익 성장 기반을 마련할 수 있다는 분석이다.

DS투자증권은 동아에스티에 대해 투자의견 매수와 목표주가 5만원을 제시했다.

출처: 핀포인트뉴스

Specializes in fast-reading probe thermometers

According to the latest IndexBox report on the global Portable Digital Thermometer market, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture.

The global portable digital thermometer market is a mature, high-volume consumer goods category defined by a bifurcation between commoditized, price-driven volume and premiumized, benefit-driven growth segments. Consumer need states have evolved beyond basic fever detection into two primary value pools: a low-engagement, replacement-driven commodity segment and a high-engagement, wellness-oriented premium segment focused on speed, accuracy, connectivity, and user experience.

Channel strategy is the primary determinant of market share, with mass-market and grocery channels dominated by private-label and value-tier brands, while pharmacy, specialty baby, and health and wellness channels serve as the battleground for branded premiumization. E-commerce has reshaped the category as both an infinite shelf for long-tail SKUs and a discovery platform for premium products, while increasing price transparency and competitive intensity. The supply chain is highly globalized, with significant manufacturing concentration creating a low-cost base but vulnerability to input cost volatility.

Brand equity is increasingly built on verifiable claims such as measurement speed, hospital-grade accuracy, and app integration. Private-label penetration is significant and growing, exerting downward pressure on branded margins. The long-term outlook is for steady, low-single-digit volume growth driven by household penetration and replacement, with value growth contingent on premium segment expansion and migration of connected health features into the mainstream.

The baseline scenario for the global portable digital thermometer market through 2035 anticipates steady, low-single-digit volume growth, underpinned by household penetration gains in emerging markets and replacement demand in mature markets. Value growth is expected to outpace volume, supported by the continued premiumization of the category as consumers trade up to devices offering faster read times, higher accuracy, and connected health features such as app integration and Bluetooth data logging. The market is projected to expand at a CAGR of approximately 3.2% in value terms from 2026 to 2035, with the market index reaching 137 (2025=100).

item.title: Ghana validates updated health data safeguards - Digital Watch Observatory
item.description:
요약

  • Ghana validates updated health data safeguards
  • Ghana validated health data guidelines covering patient access, approved data reuse, breach response and electronic records, with management approval pending.
  • They will then be submitted to Ghana Health Service management for approval before a national launch and distribution to districts and health facilities.

본문

Ghana validates updated health data safeguards

Ghana validated health data guidelines covering patient access, approved data reuse, breach response and electronic records, with management approval pending.

Ghana Health Service validated an updated health data and health records strategy and operational guidelines on 24 November 2026, according to a WHO announcement published the following day. The World Health Organisation (WHO) provided technical support, with funding from Japan. The work forms part of the AI in Health Project. It responds to growing digitalisation within healthcare.

The documents clarify patients’ access to their medical information. They also require documented approval for secondary uses of identifiable patient data. Guidance covers breach response and the management of electronic and paper records. It addresses system downtime and migration between platforms.

A review identified gaps in the existing guidelines and informed technical consultations that began in June 2026. Further consultations at regional and district levels helped refine the documents before validation. The final versions will incorporate priority recommendations from the validation workshop. They will then be submitted to Ghana Health Service management for approval before a national launch and distribution to districts and health facilities.

Why does it matter?

Patients’ information increasingly moves between digital systems supporting healthcare. Clear access and reuse procedures help facilities protect that information. Breach response arrangements establish how institutions should handle incidents involving patient records. Together, these measures connect digital health expansion with accountability for data use.

item.description:
요약

  • Can AI-Driven Nutrition Truly Transform Indian Health?
  • The integration of modern technology into lifestyle management has accelerated the adoption of AI-driven nutrition across India. In fact, healthcare practitioners now observe patients frequently turning to algorithmic mobile applications to track meals and count calories.
  • Therefore, medical experts emphasize that computational dietary interventions must unite scientific validation with regional culinary habits.

본문

Medical Updates

Can AI-Driven Nutrition Truly Transform Indian Health?

The integration of modern technology into lifestyle management has accelerated the adoption of AI-driven nutrition across India. In fact, healthcare practitioners now observe patients frequently turning to algorithmic mobile applications to track meals and count calories. However, digital meal logging alone cannot resolve the complex cardiometabolic challenges prevalent across diverse Indian demographics. Therefore, medical experts emphasize that computational dietary interventions must unite scientific validation with regional culinary habits.

The Clinical Need for AI-Driven Nutrition in India

India faces an escalating burden of cardiometabolic conditions, including type 2 diabetes and dyslipidemia. Consequently, clinicians encounter high rates of insulin resistance in routine outpatient consultations. Traditional Indian meals feature vast regional variations, complex spice mixtures, and variable carbohydrate preparations. Because generic international algorithms fail to recognize these culinary nuances, foreign software often delivers impractical clinical guidance. Furthermore, commercial health trends frequently fixate on isolated macronutrients. Dr. Naval Kishore Vikram from AIIMS New Delhi cautions against an excessive focus on single nutrients like protein. Instead, he advocates for a balanced, food-first philosophy that prioritizes total dietary quality. AI systems must therefore analyze holistic eating patterns rather than single nutrient metrics.

Computational Gastronomy and Cultural Food Science

Dietary recommendations require cultural relevance to achieve sustained patient compliance. As Dr. Ganesh Bagler explains, computational gastronomy bridges data-driven analytics with culinary heritage. This emerging discipline examines recipes, spice pairings, and molecular flavors through artificial intelligence. In addition, computational modeling helps researchers optimize nutrient retention during traditional food preparation. However, newly formulated recipes require rigorous clinical verification before medical professionals can recommend them to vulnerable patients. Moreover, public health experts emphasize the importance of breaking clinical data silos. Dr. Mona Duggal of the ICMR National Institute for Research in Digital Health stresses the need to merge public and private data streams. Consequently, unified databases can empower scalable, population-specific interventions for both rural and urban centers.

item.title: Five apps, three pharmacists and one elusive code - Health Services Daily
item.description:
요약

  • Won’t someone just dial down the digital friction and give me my Active Script List code?
  • Maybe it’s the frustrated rebel in me, but I can’t get enough of poor UX design or deliberate misuse of technology.
  • Still hopeful that I could get my ASL code, I phoned a second big-chain pharmacy and asked how to access the code.

본문

Won’t someone just dial down the digital friction and give me my Active Script List code?

Maybe it’s the frustrated rebel in me, but I can’t get enough of poor UX design or deliberate misuse of technology.

Because no matter how much work and testing is put into developing a new tool or product, how useful it is all comes down to the user.

Humans simply have a way of getting in the way of a designer’s best intentions, making a mockery of a tool’s painstakingly designed features with just a few “incorrect” interactions.

Take the brilliantly hilarious square hole challenge, for instance.

I also happen to know that if your older brother is a software engineer, it’s very entertaining if you intentionally push the wrong buttons on his new game design.

But when are technology issues a single user error and when is it a broader usability issue?

Which brings me to my recent attempt to get hold of my Active Script List code, inspired by Mina Giang’s excellent piece and my regular frustration with losing eScript texts.

(Although frankly, I felt a little called out by Ms Giang when she described hypothetical patients standing at the pharmacy counter scrolling through their texts to find their eScript. I do that standing OUTSIDE the pharmacy, thank you very much.)

Surely, I thought, there is a better system than searching for texts, and then getting yet another text or a paper script every time I got new medication?

“The Active Script List addresses the underlying problem behind much of that frustration,” Ms Giang wrote.

“Delete the message and the script is still there. Open the list and what’s current is in front of you.”

The Active Script List is a code that opens up access to all your prescriptions, no matter whether they’ve been dispensed or not, or which pharmacist has dispensed them.

I’m in, I thought. Sign me up.

And maybe it would bring more “interoperability” into my life, which is my editor Cate Swannell’s absolute favourite word of all time.

[Editor’s note: Soooooo not.]

With my sights set on getting my very own ASL code, I went to my local pharmacy and asked if I could somehow (help, please) sign up and get my Active Script List code.

But there was confusion from staff, who had to wait for the pharmacist.

In the meantime, two dads from my kids’ school happened to walk into the pharmacy, both with eScript issues.

One couldn’t find his eScript and the other had lost his paper script, and they both needed the pharmacist to look up their files. Meanwhile, another customer overheard my conversation with the pharmacist and suggested I use the 1800MEDICARE app.

The pharmacist gave me the name of a medication management app and a code which she said was linked to the pharmacy.

Ms Giang had warned about this when she said: “There are two different codes a pharmacy can hand over, and they do very different jobs.

“One activates that pharmacy’s app. The other unlocks your Active Script List, in whichever conformant app you choose.

item.title: Changing Faces – Digital and supplier hires, October 2026 - pharmaphorum
item.description:
요약

  • Changing Faces – Digital and supplier hires, October 2026
  • October saw the usual number of leadership changes in the digital health and pharmaceutical supplier sectors.
  • - The company appointed Ali Tafreshi as CEO. The chief strategy officer for Topcon Corp.'s Eyecare Business Division, Tafreshi previously served as global head and VP of product management and clinical affairs at Heidelberg Engineering.

본문

Changing Faces – Digital and supplier hires, October 2026

October saw the usual number of leadership changes in the digital health and pharmaceutical supplier sectors.

Read on for the full round-up.

Oku Digital Health unveils star-studded founding team. AI-powered digital health company Oku Digital Health officially launched from Topcon Healthcare with a founding executive team drawn from across healthcare, technology, and life sciences. The company launched with the aim of turning routine eye examinations into a real-time gateway for broader healthcare interventions and drug development through AI-powered technologies.

- The company appointed Ali Tafreshi as CEO. The chief strategy officer for Topcon Corp.'s Eyecare Business Division, Tafreshi previously served as global head and VP of product management and clinical affairs at Heidelberg Engineering.

- Trent Norris takes on the role of chief operating officer after serving as global head of business development for digital health at NVIDIA, alongside previous leadership positions at Flywheel.io and Microsoft.

- The company's AI efforts were placed under the leadership of Dr Matt Lungren, who will serve as chief data AI officer. Lungren previously served as chief scientific officer at Microsoft Health & Life Sciences and also holds an academic appointment as adjunct professor at Stanford University School of Medicine.

- Dr Daniela Ferrara was appointed chief medical officer. In addition to serving as assistant professor at Tufts University School of Medicine, she previously worked as principal medical director of ophthalmology at Genentech.

- Completing the founding leadership team, Jacques Gilbert joined as chief strategy and business development officer. Gilbert previously served as VP of healthcare strategy, partnerships, and M&A at Microsoft and also held senior roles at Nuance Communications and GE Healthcare.

eClinical Solutions expands executive leadership team. Global digital clinical software and services provider eClinical Solutions announced three senior appointments designed to support continued growth and product innovation.

- Jessica Allen joined as chief financial officer, bringing nearly two decades of financial leadership experience. Her remit includes helping scale the business while ensuring ongoing investment in key areas for customers, employees, and future development.

- The company also appointed Brian Testa as chief people officer. With more than 20 years of leadership experience, Testa has been tasked with leading the organisation’s people and culture strategy as it continues to evolve and expand.

- Rounding out the appointments is chief product officer Nathan Johnson, who is being promoted after more than five years with the company. Johnson takes responsibility for product strategy and roadmap development, including further expansion of AI and automation capabilities.

item.title: Narrative Review Highlights Emerging Positive Outcomes of Adolescent Social Media Use - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • According to the authors, the expanding prevalence of digital technologies has made understanding their role in adolescent mental health increasingly critical, particularly in cases where a psychiatric disorder co-exists.
  • The narrative review was designed to critically and comprehensively assess the available literature concerning the potential benefits and constructive impacts of social media use across diverse groups of young people.
  • Article Title: Beyond the risks: exploring the positive influence of social media on adolescent mental health

본문

A peer-reviewed narrative review published in Child and Adolescent Psychiatry and Mental Health reports that positive outcomes related to adolescent social media use are emerging across scientific literature, accompanied by ongoing discussions regarding the potential integration of digital technologies into clinical care.

According to the authors, the expanding prevalence of digital technologies has made understanding their role in adolescent mental health increasingly critical, particularly in cases where a psychiatric disorder co-exists. While earlier research and existing publications have extensively documented the negative consequences associated with unsafe social media use, scholarly attention has increasingly shifted toward investigating beneficial dimensions following the widespread social isolation enforced during the COVID-19 pandemic.

The narrative review was designed to critically and comprehensively assess the available literature concerning the potential benefits and constructive impacts of social media use across diverse groups of young people. The examination encompassed healthy adolescents, adolescents carrying psychiatric disorders, and youth who have witnessed a traumatic experience, evaluating how digital engagement relates to their overall well-being.

To identify relevant evidence on social media use and youth well-being, the researchers gathered and analyzed studies from major scientific databases alongside grey literature sources.

Subject of Research: Positive effects of social media use on adolescent mental health

Article Title: Beyond the risks: exploring the positive influence of social media on adolescent mental health

item.title: Govt clarifies SHA digital health levy, maintains Sh800,000 cancer treatment benefit - Education News
item.description:
요약

  • The government has moved to address mounting concerns over the Social Health Authority (SHA), offering fresh explanations on the controversial digital health levy and the management of cancer treatment benefits.
  • Government Spokesperson Charles Owino said the administration was reviewing aspects of the healthcare financing system to strengthen transparency, improve hospital accountability and shield patients from unnecessary medical costs.
  • Speaking during a media briefing in Nairobi on Thursday, November 26, 2026, Owino addressed questions surrounding the two per cent Health Information Management System (HIMS) utilisation fee charged on SHA pre-authorised claims.

본문

The government has moved to address mounting concerns over the Social Health Authority (SHA), offering fresh explanations on the controversial digital health levy and the management of cancer treatment benefits.

Government Spokesperson Charles Owino said the administration was reviewing aspects of the healthcare financing system to strengthen transparency, improve hospital accountability and shield patients from unnecessary medical costs.

Speaking during a media briefing in Nairobi on Thursday, November 26, 2026, Owino addressed questions surrounding the two per cent Health Information Management System (HIMS) utilisation fee charged on SHA pre-authorised claims.

The issue has attracted public attention following a High Court ruling in Vihiga that declared the levy invalid. However, the court suspended the declaration for 120 days, giving the Health Cabinet Secretary time to undertake public participation before proceeding with further action.

Owino said the government would abide by the court’s directions while continuing to invest in digital systems intended to improve healthcare delivery.

State defends Sh104.8 billion digital health project

The spokesperson also defended the Sh104.8 billion Digital Health Superhighway, clarifying that the initiative operates through a service-based arrangement rather than the conventional purchase of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) equipment.

Launched in February 2025, the 10-year programme is being implemented by a consortium involving Safaricom, Apeiro Limited and Konvergenz Network Solutions.

The government says the digital infrastructure is designed to improve patient identification, streamline electronic claims, enhance medical records management and strengthen the monitoring of medicines across healthcare facilities.

The system is also expected to help identify fraudulent claims and improve accountability in the utilisation of public healthcare resources.

Government denies reduction of cancer treatment benefits

Owino further addressed concerns among cancer patients following changes in the administration of treatment approvals and payments under SHA.

He maintained that the Sh800,000 cancer treatment benefit per patient remains intact, dismissing concerns that the approved package had been reduced.

The benefit is structured into two allocations: Sh400,000 from the Social Health Insurance Fund (SHIF) and another Sh400,000 from the Emergency, Critical and Chronic Illness Fund (ECCIF).

According to Owino, the review was informed by significant variations in hospital charges for similar cancer treatment procedures, which sometimes resulted in patients exhausting their benefits before completing treatment.

The revised framework seeks to harmonise treatment costs, promote consistency in hospital billing and ensure patients receive the full value of their available coverage.

item.description:
요약

  • Digital NHS: over 9,000 facilities connected, but significant disparities between regions and generations
  • Gimbe report: the infrastructure figures are positive, but the ability to integrate data and technologies into clinical and care processes needs to be assessed
  • In 2024, 7.7 per cent of people aged 75 and over booked an appointment with a healthcare professional online, compared with 38.7 per cent of 35–44-year-olds.

본문

Digital NHS: over 9,000 facilities connected, but significant disparities between regions and generations

Gimbe report: the infrastructure figures are positive, but the ability to integrate data and technologies into clinical and care processes needs to be assessed

The National Health Service is undergoing a rapid digital transformation, which is, however, progressing at different speeds across the country. Italians’ digital skills also remain below the European average, whilst the use of the electronic health record shows extreme regional variations. These are the key issues at the heart of the Gimbe Foundation’s analysis, presented by its president Nino Cartabellotta at the Healthcare Risk Management Forum in Arezzo, an event which marks the conclusion of its latest Tuscan edition: the event has been acquired by VeronaFiere and will move to the Veneto region.

“The pace of technological development,” said Gimbe’s president, Cartabellotta, “is far outstripping the ability of healthcare systems to adapt to digital transformation. We need vision, investment in infrastructure, digital literacy and training for healthcare professionals, as well as bold reforms. Otherwise, the gap between technological innovation and the benefits for citizens and the National Health Service will continue to widen, exacerbating inequalities.”

Over 9,000 connected premises with a speed of at least 1 Gbps

The ‘Connected Healthcare’ Plan, funded by Mission 1 of the NRRP, has connected 9,254 healthcare facilities with speeds of at least 1 Gbps, according to the eighth Report to Parliament on the NRRP. This is 554 more facilities than the target of 8,700 (+6.4 per cent). “The infrastructure figures are positive,” observed Cartabellotta, “but they cannot be taken as a measure of the digital transformation of the National Health Service: a connected facility is not automatically one capable of integrating data and technologies into clinical and care processes.” According to data from the Connetti Italia portal, the highest number of healthcare facilities brought online is found in Lombardy (1,323), Piedmont (914), Veneto (910), Campania (815) and Sicily (759).

Internet usage falls from 72.5 per cent amongst 65–74-year-olds to 35.7 per cent amongst those aged 75 and over. In 2024, 7.7 per cent of people aged 75 and over booked an appointment with a healthcare professional online, compared with 38.7 per cent of 35–44-year-olds.

item.title: Government moves to address SHA concerns over fees, cancer costs - The Star, Kenya
item.description:
요약

  • The Government has outlined measures to address concerns surrounding the Social Health Authority (SHA), including compliance with court directives on digital health charges, strengthening healthcare systems and protecting patients from unnecessary medical costs.
  • Speaking during a media briefing at the Government Spokesperson Media Centre in Nairobi, Owino said the Government remained committed to complying with judicial directives concerning the two per cent Health Information Management System (HIMS) utilisation fee.
  • “Digital health systems must facilitate healthcare delivery and must not undermine the financial sustainability of the healthcare facilities,” he said.

본문

The Government has outlined measures to address concerns surrounding the Social Health Authority (SHA), including compliance with court directives on digital health charges, strengthening healthcare systems and protecting patients from unnecessary medical costs.

Government Spokesperson Charles Owino said the State was seeking to strengthen the implementation of SHA through digital infrastructure reforms, improved accountability in healthcare delivery and standardised cancer treatment costs, amid ongoing scrutiny of the health financing system.

Speaking during a media briefing at the Government Spokesperson Media Centre in Nairobi, Owino said the Government remained committed to complying with judicial directives concerning the two per cent Health Information Management System (HIMS) utilisation fee.

This follows a High Court ruling in Vihiga declaring the levy on SHA pre-authorised claims invalid. However, the court suspended the declaration for 120 days, within which the Health Cabinet Secretary may, if advised, subject the fee to public participation.

Owino reiterated that the Government would comply with the applicable court directives.

“Digital health systems must facilitate healthcare delivery and must not undermine the financial sustainability of the healthcare facilities,” he said.

The Government also defended the financing model for the Digital Health Superhighway, describing it as a service-based arrangement rather than a conventional procurement of ICT infrastructure.

“It is not a purchase. It is a service model. Instead of government buying servers, software licenses, and hiring IT staff, it is buying the outcome as a service,” Owino said.

The 10-year programme, launched in February 2025 and implemented by a consortium comprising Safaricom, Apeiro Limited and Konvergenz Network Solutions, is expected to cost Sh104.8 billion.

Under the arrangement, the consortium finances the development, installation, maintenance and support of the infrastructure, while the Government pays for services delivered through monthly payments from SHA funds.

The model covers equipment, connectivity, cloud hosting, cybersecurity, technical support, training and maintenance. The service provider is responsible for system upgrades and infrastructure maintenance throughout the contractual period, after which the system is expected to be handed over to the Government.

According to Owino, the digital infrastructure is intended to replace fragmented, paper-based healthcare processes with an integrated system that improves patient identification, claims management, medicine tracking and accountability in healthcare delivery.

The system is expected to facilitate biometric patient identification, electronic claims processing, secure exchange of medical records, provider authentication, facility registration and emergency response services, including the National Ambulance Dispatch Centre.

item.title: WeChat Mini Program Improves Older Adults’ Sarcopenia Knowledge and Behavior - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • A digital health education knowledge graph delivered through a WeChat mini program was associated with significant preliminary improvements in sarcopenia-related knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors among community-dwelling older adults.
  • Developed to address the growing threat sarcopenia poses to the physical function and quality of life of older populations, the digital platform provides an interactive health education tool tailored to community settings.
  • Article Title: Development of a health education knowledge graph for sarcopenia prevention and management among community-dwelling older adults: from knowledge modeling to WeChat mini program application

본문

A digital health education knowledge graph delivered through a WeChat mini program was associated with significant preliminary improvements in sarcopenia-related knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors among community-dwelling older adults. Developed to address the growing threat sarcopenia poses to the physical function and quality of life of older populations, the digital platform provides an interactive health education tool tailored to community settings. In an initial pre-post evaluation, older adults demonstrated statistically significant gains across all three assessed domains following system use, while reporting high overall usability ratings for the application.

Sarcopenia represents a substantial long-term burden on individuals and healthcare systems, yet accessible educational resources specifically designed for older community members remain limited. To bridge this gap, investigators carried out a comprehensive development and evaluation project spanning from October 2023 to November 2025. The research team structured the work across five continuous operational phases: knowledge graph construction, visual mapping of domain concepts, knowledge base vectorization, development of an automated question-and-answer system embedded within a WeChat mini program, and final empirical effect evaluation.

To build an authoritative domain foundation, the health education knowledge graph extracted biomedical entities and clinical relationships across twelve databases, four specialized books, seven clinical guidelines and expert consensuses, and thirty-four real-world user inquiry cases. Following systematic information extraction, the resulting knowledge graph encompassed 1,568 distinct entities and 1,599 relational connections. The synthesized knowledge structure systematically covered core dimensions of sarcopenia management, including standard disease definitions, formal diagnostic criteria, documented risk factors, validated clinical screening tools, and targeted preventive lifestyle measures.

The underlying educational content underwent rigorous verification through a formal two-round expert consultation designed to validate content relevance and confirm professional consensus. Expert review assessments yielded a judgment coefficient of 0.973, a familiarity coefficient of 0.853, and an overall authority coefficient of 0.913. Statistical evaluations using Kendall’s concordance coefficient tests were statistically significant at p < .01, confirming strong consensus across the consulting specialists. Manual annotation quality was independently verified, achieving a Fleiss’ Kappa inter-rater agreement coefficient of 0.71, indicating substantial agreement among annotators, while the overall manual annotation error rate was restricted to 9.4%, remaining safely below the established 15% acceptable threshold.
